---
name: "Backend Engineering Guidelines"
description: "Use when modifying the backend FastAPI API, services, SQLAlchemy models, Pydantic schemas, runtime, RAG, migrations, or backend tests."
applyTo: "backend/**"
---
# Backend Engineering Guidelines

- Preserve the project boundaries: keep routers in `backend/app/api/` thin (request parsing, dependency resolution, service calls, and responses); put use cases, authorization, ownership checks, and transaction boundaries in `backend/app/services/`. Keep ORM models in `backend/app/models/`, Pydantic contracts in `backend/app/schemas/`, session setup in `backend/app/database.py`, shared text processing in `backend/app/rag/`, and agent orchestration in `backend/app/runtime/`.
- Follow neighboring code: use async functions for API, database, and provider I/O; SQLAlchemy 2.x `select` and `Mapped` patterns; UUIDs; and explicit type hints. Inject sessions and replaceable providers through constructors or FastAPI dependencies rather than creating module-level clients or sessions in business logic.
- Enforce authorization in service queries, not only at the router. Scope every user-owned resource to its authenticated owner and verify relationships across nested resources such as agents, conversations, documents, skills, and tools. Never trust client-provided owner IDs. Use the existing admin dependency for admin-only catalog operations.
- Preserve route prefixes, response models, status codes, and generated OpenAPI behavior. Keep endpoints under `/api/v1`, except for the intentional unprefixed `/health` endpoint. Update focused API tests when a contract changes.
- Keep database models, schemas, and migrations consistent. Add schema changes as new Alembic revisions in `backend/migrations/versions/`; do not edit migrations that may already have been applied. Include reversible operations where practical and verify relationship cascades for model changes.
- Keep `AgentRuntime` as the orchestration layer. Put provider-specific LLM behavior in `backend/app/runtime/llm.py`, retrieval in `backend/app/runtime/rag.py`, tool execution in `backend/app/runtime/tools.py`, and skill ranking in `backend/app/runtime/skills.py`. Reuse `backend/app/rag/` helpers for shared text cleaning, chunking, and embeddings; keep retrieval agent-scoped and use the agent's configured thresholds and top-k settings.
- Treat persisted tool metadata as declarative. Execute tools only through handlers registered in the process-local tool registry; validate inputs and outputs and preserve execution timeouts and failure-as-result behavior. Do not execute database strings as code.
- Keep external providers replaceable so tests can use deterministic fakes. Never hard-code or expose `.env` values, API keys, JWT secrets, database credentials, or other secrets. Avoid logging credentials, tokens, sensitive prompts, or full document contents.
- Add or update focused `pytest` coverage for behavior changes, especially authentication and ownership, nested-resource access, provider failures, runtime orchestration, and migrations. Prefer lightweight fakes over live OpenAI or PostgreSQL dependencies in unit tests.
- Run the fast backend suite from the repository root with `py -m pytest backend/tests -q`. For API contract coverage, follow `backend/docs/API_TESTING.md`. For schema changes, verify the new migration against the configured development database; do not weaken application validation to work around missing environment configuration.
